rewrites.prompt: A logistics firm's labour turnover has risen from 7.5% two years ago to 14.0% this year. Explain what this comparison tells its managers.
rewrites.canonical_answer: Compared with its own past, the firm is now losing roughly twice the share of its workforce each year: on an average headcount of 240 that is about 34 leavers instead of 18. That means extra recruitment and training spending - at about N$12 000 to replace and retrain a driver, 16 extra leavers cost roughly N$192 000 a year. What the comparison does not tell managers is why people are leaving, so they would need to compare the rate with other local logistics firms, and use exit interviews and pay comparisons, before choosing a response.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the point identified - turnover has roughly doubled against the firm's own earlier rate.

2 marks (AO2): the comparison applied - about 34 leavers instead of 18 and roughly N$192 000 a year of extra replacement cost, with the limitation that the rate carries no cause; 1 mark if the rates are restated without their meaning.
Comparison: against the firm's own past and, ideally, other local employers. Meaning: what the change implies for the firm.
rewrites.why: State is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks, one point applied to the firm's figures.

rewrites.prompt: Kalahari Freight employs an average of 240 people, and 18 of them left last year. Explain the difference between its labour turnover and the number of employees who left.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The number of leavers is a count of people; labour turnover is a rate - that count expressed as a percentage of the average number employed over the same period. For Kalahari Freight the count is 18 leavers and the turnover is 18 / 240 x 100, which is 7.5%. The count tells the firm how many replacements it must recruit this year. The rate is what it can compare, because a depot of 60 people losing the same 18 would have turnover of 30% and a far more serious problem.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - a count of leavers against a rate expressed as a percentage of the average workforce.

2 marks (AO2): the difference applied to Kalahari Freight - 18 leavers against turnover of 7.5%, and what each is used for (the count sizes recruitment, the rate allows comparison); 1 mark if applied without the figures.
Boundary: the denominator must be named, because it is what turns the count into a rate.

rewrites.prompt: A Swakopmund hotel is recruiting a night receptionist. Explain the difference between the job description and the person specification it should prepare for the post.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The job description describes the post; the person specification describes the person the post needs. For the night receptionist, the job description would set out the duties - checking in late arrivals, running the night audit, responding to alarms - the reporting line to the duty manager and the hours, and it stays true whoever holds the job. The person specification would set out what the hotel screens applicants against: front-desk experience, confidence in handling payments, and the reliability to work alone overnight. A statement that would still be true if nobody held the job belongs in the job description.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - one describes the post, the other the holder the post needs.
2 marks (AO2): the difference applied to the night receptionist post - duties and conditions on one side, the screening criteria on the other; 1 mark for a generic contrast.
Boundary: describing the post against describing the holder.

rewrites.prompt: The head chef of a Windhoek restaurant has resigned. The restaurant could promote its sous-chef or advertise the post. Explain the difference between internal and external recruitment for this vacancy.
rewrites.canonical_answer: Internal recruitment fills the vacancy from people the business already employs; external recruitment fills it from applicants who do not work there. If the restaurant promotes its sous-chef, it already holds years of evidence about how she cooks and runs a kitchen, and she knows the menu and the suppliers - but her promotion leaves the sous-chef post to fill as well. An external head chef would be judged on an application and a trial shift and would have the kitchen and its systems to learn, though the restaurant would face no second vacancy and could gain new dishes and methods.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - where the appointee comes from.

2 marks (AO2): the difference applied to this kitchen - the evidence the restaurant already holds on the sous-chef and the second vacancy her promotion creates, against the external candidate; 1 mark if only one side is applied.
Boundary: the source of the appointee, developed into its consequences.

rewrites.prompt: A Walvis Bay fishing company expects about 150 applications for 20 deckhand posts. Explain the difference between asking applicants to complete an application form and asking them to send a curriculum vitae.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is who writes the document. An application form is written by the employer and completed in the same way by every applicant; a curriculum vitae is written by the applicant in their own format. With 150 applicants for 20 posts, a form would let the company compare everyone point by point - sea experience, safety certificates, any gap between jobs - and force answers a curriculum vitae might leave out. A curriculum vitae would be quicker for applicants to send, so it could attract more of them, but each would show only what that applicant chose to present, which makes the shortlist harder to draw up.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - authorship: the employer's questions against the applicant's own document.
2 marks (AO2): the difference applied to 150 applications for 20 deckhand posts - comparability and completeness against a larger field at lower effort; 1 mark for a generic contrast.
Boundary: who writes the document, followed into its consequences.

rewrites.prompt: A Windhoek accounting firm is choosing a bookkeeper who will work mostly in spreadsheets. Explain the difference between the evidence an interview and a selection test would give the firm.
rewrites.canonical_answer: An interview gives evidence of what an applicant says - how they describe their experience and reason through a question. A test gives evidence of what the applicant can do, scored the same way for everyone. For the bookkeeper's post the difference matters: an applicant can describe their spreadsheet skills convincingly and still fail a timed spreadsheet exercise, so the test measures the skill the firm needs directly, while the interview can only infer it. The interview still earns its place, because it shows how the applicant handles a follow-up question from a client, which no fixed test can do.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - reported ability against demonstrated ability.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the bookkeeper's post - the spreadsheet test measures the core skill directly, the interview reaches what a test cannot; 1 mark if one side only.
Boundary: what each source of evidence can show, with a genuine strength kept on both sides.
rewrites.why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

rewrites.prompt: A Rundu transport company is about to appoint a driver whose curriculum vitae lists eight years of accident-free driving. Explain the difference between the evidence a reference and the curriculum vitae give the company.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is who makes the claim. The curriculum vitae is the driver's own account, so the eight accident-free years are claimed by the person whose record is in question. A reference comes from someone else - a previous employer who saw that driving over years - so the company uses it to check the claim rather than to add to it. The reference has limits too: the driver chose the referees, and many employers confirm only dates and job title in writing, so the company may need to ask the referee directly about accidents and reliability.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - a self-made claim against a third party's account.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the driver - the reference is used to verify the eight accident-free years, with its limits (chosen referees, limited disclosure); 1 mark for a generic contrast.
Boundary: who makes the claim; neither document is treated as simply reliable.

rewrites.prompt: A Keetmanshoop clinic is hiring a receptionist. One applicant's form shows a typing certificate gained six years ago. Explain the difference between what a typing test and the application form tell the clinic about this applicant.
rewrites.canonical_answer: An application form reports the applicant's history - qualifications held, jobs done, dates worked. A test shows what the applicant can do now, under conditions the clinic sets. For this applicant the two can disagree: a typing certificate from six years ago is evidence of past skill, not proof that it has been kept up, whereas a short typing test measures her speed and accuracy today. The form still covers ground the test does not, such as her employment history and why she left her last job, and it costs the clinic far less to use.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - a record of the past against a performance in the present.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the six-year-old certificate - the test checks whether the skill has been kept up, the form covers history the test cannot; 1 mark if one side only.
Boundary: reported history against present performance.

rewrites.prompt: A construction firm in Oshakati needs extra site supervisors for an 18-month school-building project. Explain the difference between offering them permanent and fixed-term contracts.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is whether an end is written into the contract. A permanent contract has no end date and continues until one side ends it; a fixed-term contract ends on a stated date or when a stated task is complete. For an 18-month project, a fixed-term contract limits the firm's wage commitment to the period the supervisors are needed, whereas permanent contracts would leave it paying them after the school is finished unless it has further work for them. The supervisors would see it the other way round: the permanent contract gives steady income and security, the fixed-term one certain income only until the project ends.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - whether an end date is written into the engagement.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the 18-month project - the firm's commitment and the supervisors' security; 1 mark if only one side is applied.
Boundary: an end written in or not, followed into its consequences.

rewrites.prompt: A Luderitz fish processor is closing its canning line. It is also dealing with an employee on the filleting line who has repeatedly failed hygiene checks. Explain the difference between redundancy and dismissal in these two cases.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is what has come to an end. In redundancy the post has gone and the person was adequate; in dismissal the post remains and the person was not. The canning-line workers are redundant: their jobs disappear with the line, so the processor needs stated selection criteria and consultation, and they would normally be entitled to a redundancy payment. The filleting-line employee faces dismissal: the job continues, so the processor needs an investigation, warnings and a hearing about her failed hygiene checks, and an employee fairly dismissed would normally receive no redundancy payment.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - whether the post survives.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the two cases - procedure and payment for the canning-line workers against the filleting-line employee; 1 mark if only one case is handled.
Boundary: whether the post survives, followed into procedure and payment.
rewrites.why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

rewrites.prompt: A Tsumeb mine must cut 60 of its 400 jobs. Explain the difference between voluntary and involuntary redundancy as ways of reaching that number.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is who decides which individuals leave. In voluntary redundancy the mine announces that 60 posts must go and invites employees to volunteer, normally in return for a payment above the minimum. In involuntary redundancy the mine selects the 60 itself, using criteria stated in advance such as length of service, the skills it will still need and attendance records. Voluntary redundancy avoids disputes over whether the selection was fair, but the mine may lose experienced electricians it wanted to keep; compulsory redundancy lets it keep the skills it needs, at the cost of a harder consultation.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - who chooses the individuals who leave.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the 60 posts - no dispute about selection against control over which skills stay; 1 mark if one side only.
Boundary: who chooses, with a consequence on each side.
rewrites.why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

rewrites.prompt: A Windhoek call centre employs staff who speak eight different home languages, but all twelve of its team leaders come from one of those language groups. Explain the difference between diversity and equality, using this workplace.
rewrites.canonical_answer: Diversity describes what a workforce looks like - how far its members differ in background, language, age and experience. Equality describes how decisions about the workforce are made: recruitment, pay, training and promotion based on what the job requires rather than on characteristics unrelated to it. The call centre shows the two coming apart. With eight home languages among its staff it is diverse, but all twelve team leaders coming from one group raises the question of whether promotion is decided on what the job requires, so diversity is present without clear evidence of equality.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - the composition of the workforce against the basis of decisions about it.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the call centre - a varied workforce whose promotions raise a question about equality; 1 mark for a generic contrast.
Boundary: composition against the basis of decisions; the two can come apart.

rewrites.prompt: A new sales assistant is starting at an Ondangwa furniture store. Explain the difference between her induction training and the on-the-job and off-the-job training she may also receive.
rewrites.canonical_answer: Induction is defined by when it happens: at the start of employment, covering the business, the post, the people and health and safety. On-the-job and off-the-job training are defined by where they happen - at the work position or away from it. So for the new sales assistant they are not three alternatives. In her first days her induction would introduce the store, its staff and its safety rules; she might then learn the stock system on the job beside an experienced colleague, or attend a supplier's product course off the job. Her induction itself could contain both kinds.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - a form defined by timing against forms defined by location.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the new sales assistant - induction first, then training in the skills of the post, on or off the job; 1 mark for a generic contrast.
Boundary: timing against location; the three are not alternatives for one need.
rewrites.why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

rewrites.prompt: A Walvis Bay engineering workshop needs its apprentices to learn to weld to a certified standard. Explain the difference between on-the-job and off-the-job training for them.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is where the learning happens and whether the apprentice is producing while it does. On the job, an apprentice learns at the workshop bench beside an experienced welder, so some output continues and what is learned fits the workshop's own equipment and jobs - but the experienced welder produces less while teaching. Off the job, the apprentice attends a training centre and produces nothing for the workshop during the course, but gains certified instructors and a recognised qualification the workshop cannot award itself. So one carries a hidden cost in lost output and the other a visible cost in fees and absence.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - location, and whether output continues.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the welding apprentices - workshop-specific learning and the trainer's lost output against certification, fees and absence; 1 mark if one side only.
Boundary: where the learning happens, followed into its cost.
rewrites.why: Distinguish is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain at 3 marks - one difference, taken into a named business.

rewrites.prompt: A Windhoek bank teaches its tellers a new cash-handling system and also sends some of them on a management course. Explain the difference between training and employee development in this bank.
rewrites.canonical_answer: The difference is what each is aimed at. Training is aimed at the job the employee holds now and is judged by whether they do that job better; development is aimed at roles the employee could fill later and is judged by whether the business has people ready when a larger post opens. Teaching the tellers the new cash-handling system is training: it succeeds if errors and queue times fall this quarter. The management course is development: it succeeds if the bank can fill a branch supervisor's post from its own tellers in two or three years rather than recruiting from outside.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the difference identified - the current job against future roles.
2 marks (AO2): applied to the bank - the cash-handling system judged by current performance, the management course by who is ready for promotion; 1 mark if one side only.
Boundary: current job against future roles, with how each is judged.
